title: Read-only qualification: 4-6h real process, zero writes
description:
Run the real one-market process for a supervised 4–6 hour operating window with H-VER-1 unarmed. This is a read-only operational qualification, not the promotion gate for the later writer. It proves that the nominated commit can observe the real account, restart from its durable paths, remain monitored, and expose every attempted write without any network non-GET call.

Use the actual launchd/caffeinate supervision, five-record store, alert channel and external dead man. Force at least one websocket disconnect/quarantine/reconnect/resnapshot/reconcile and one process death/restart using the same durable paths. A safely forced event may discover and fail a missing relay; q01 does not require unrelated exchange write-response behavior to be implemented before the observer is allowed to run.

Owner-only stall and exchange schedule/host-clock jump remain deterministic promotion scenarios, not q01 live drills. The production binary has no safe external mechanism to freeze one goroutine or make the exchange change its schedule, and changing the host clock is not a defensible real-account test. q01 still exercises ordinary schedule polling and proves the real monitor/heartbeat paths continue.

Require at least 99% monitor availability against elapsed-time cadence, fresh complete position/order/fill walks, continuing heartbeat in every reached global state, bounded durable would-write and attempted-method evidence, and no silent anomaly loss. Preserve the compact qualification bundle.

No agent executes this bead against the real account. Live-account execution, forced external events and alarm confirmation are operator actions.
acceptance_criteria:
Attach start/end timestamps, exact commit and config hash, actual transport method counts measured below the write guard, attempted methods measured above it, disconnect/reconnect/reconcile timestamps, state/anomaly summary, monitor/portfolio freshness evidence, committed-run restart linkage, bounded would-write episodes, heartbeat/dead-man check-in evidence, and proof that the external missed-heartbeat alarm fired.

The assessor requires at least four hours of linked monotonic active time; the operator plans an orderly end by six hours. Running long does not retroactively falsify safety evidence, so six hours is an operating cutoff rather than a qualification loophole or a machine failure condition. Any network non-GET call, unexplained SEV1, anomaly-drop evidence, cadence-adjusted monitor ratio below 99%, incomplete/stale portfolio coverage, missed heartbeat, incomplete adoption/reconciliation, corrupt evidence bundle, unlinked segment, or unbounded local reservation/evidence growth fails qualification. The complete mutation catalogue must be green on the exact nominated commit before the operator starts it.
notes:
Candidate identity for the q01 attempt (prepared 2026-08-12, not yet started).

  nominated commit  dc77e3f  (the commit lip-jy4 closed GREEN, 273/273)
  binary            /Users/hugh/.lip/bin/harness
  binary sha256     1882b82fbec9c00aeb683086fb2d1e11a86cbcd7fff0462b96dfba3fdd8d0cf1
  built from        /Users/hugh/kek/lip-q01-build/go  (detached worktree at
                    dc77e3f, tree verified clean at build time)
  toolchain         go1.26.4
  config            /Users/hugh/.lip/canary/config.json
  ticker            KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE
  evidence bundle   /Users/hugh/.lip/canary/q01-evidence.json
  launchd label     com.lip.harness
  runbook           /Users/hugh/.lip/q01-runbook.md

BINARY IDENTITY IS THE SHA256 ALONE. This repo's module lives in go/ while the
git root is one level up, and under that layout Go emits no vcs.revision /
vcs.modified build setting even when -buildvcs=true is passed explicitly --
verified, no error and no stamp. So currentBinaryIdentity()
(cmd/harness/qualification.go:144) appends nothing to the hash. Two consequences
worth recording here rather than rediscovering later:

  - The dirty working tree at build time (.beads/interactions.jsonl modified,
    .codex-handoff/ untracked) could not have contaminated the evidence bundle.
    That risk does not exist under this layout.
  - The commit linkage is an operator assertion, not a self-attestation by the
    binary -- but it is checkable, because the build is deterministic. Checking
    out dc77e3f to /Users/hugh/kek/lip-q01-build and running
    `go build -o <out> ./cmd/harness` from go/ under go1.26.4 reproduces
    1882b82f... byte for byte; two independent builds already did. The path
    matters: without -trimpath the build directory is embedded.

CONFIG. Byte-identical to the reviewed config.example.json apart from `ticker`,
so the template's "a diff of the file against an empty one is the whole config
review" property holds. s=1 canary, so no -rung flag is required (main.go:370).

TICKER SELECTION. The active LIP universe is 3,245 markets across 4 pages.
score.py, q1select.py and the lip.db collector all read ONE page of 200 with no
cursor, so every view built on them is truncated; cmd/harness does a complete
cursor walk (harness/rest/read.go:630) and refuses to start on a ticker outside
the complete set. Membership was therefore re-tested against the complete walk,
which KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE passes. A lip.db-based reading that showed
this ticker present in only 17 of 61 recent snapshots was a paging artifact, not
a membership lapse.

The hazard the choice is made against is a programme lapsing ACROSS THE MANDATED
RESTART DRILL: every restart re-runs the active-programme walk, and a ticker that
has fallen out by then turns KeepAlive:true into a respawn loop against a start
refusal, with the run dead and nothing reporting it. This ticker's programme end
and market close are both 2026-09-03T14:00Z -- 22 days of runway, so neither can
fire inside a 4-6h window. Book traffic is not a qualification risk: the monitor
ticks at 1 Hz unconditionally (cmd/harness/monitor.go:65), so slot freshness
comes from the harness's own cadence and not from market activity.

TWO OPERATING TRAPS recorded before the run rather than after:

  - The restart drill must SIGKILL the harness CHILD, by pid. The launchd job's
    argv is `/usr/bin/caffeinate -is <harness> ...`
    (harness/lifecycle/launchd.go:125), so caffeinate is the process launchd
    tracks and harness is its child. `pkill -f harness` matches both, and
    SIGKILLing caffeinate orphans a still-running harness while launchd starts a
    second one, which the instance lock then refuses in a respawn loop. SIGTERM
    is also wrong: it sets WINDING_DOWN and commits a durable stop
    (main.go:300-307), which would make the rest of the window a wind-down
    rather than an observation.
  - paths.stop cannot end the run. It is Section 12's out-of-band halt and
    explicitly not a drain (config.go:148-161): it stops the harness adding and
    can never end the process. The orderly end is
    `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.lip.harness`.

Editing the config or rebuilding the binary between deploy and assessment makes
every restart fail with ErrMetadataMismatch (harness/qual/recorder.go:307),
which under KeepAlive is a silent respawn loop. Nothing changes mid-run.

Start was blocked by lip-83o: LaunchdPlan.Render() writes booleans as <true></true> and launchd rejects that form with 'Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error', so -deploy's plist has never been loadable. Isolated by single-variable probe agents; only the tag form predicts the failure. Working around it operator-side in ~/.lip/q01.sh, which runs plutil -convert xml1 over the installed plist before bootstrapping and asserts no paired booleans remain. The conversion is semantics-preserving -- ProgramArguments verified byte-identical across it -- so the deployed argv is still exactly what installAgent wrote, and the run's identity is unaffected. No Go was edited, so the mutation catalogue that closed lip-jy4 against dc77e3f still holds.
ATTEMPT 1 ABORTED 2026-08-12T17:33Z after ~3 minutes, on lip-9tr. Portfolio slots read observed 12 / fresh_complete 0 / incomplete_walks 12 while monitor slots were a clean 60/60, so the local bar was already unreachable and six hours would only have produced a guaranteed failure. Cause is real exchange data: fill 1582884a-1f64-7c20-fab4-b40468ad5df6 carries fee_cost "0.017200", six decimals, and portfolio.go:564 parses fee_cost with rest.ParsePrice4, whose measured quantum is 1e-4 dollars. convertFills errors, FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE SEV1 fires, the whole walk is discarded and the fills freshness clock does not advance -- once per 5s poll, permanently, because the fill is historical and appears in every complete walk. No operational workaround exists. The alert path worked correctly throughout: the SEV1 was delivered to the operator's phone with urgent priority within seconds, alongside the STARTUP summary and a SEV2 RESNAPSHOT_DEFERRED.

dependencies.title: EPIC CR-1: one-market continuous runtime
dependencies.description:
CR-1 means one operator-selected active-program market at S=12 may repeat
maker-entry, reduction, flat and requote cycles without synchronous operator
involvement during one declared market assignment. It runs under launchd and
caffeinate, survives process and websocket restarts through safe adoption, and
either continues safely or durably enters WINDING_DOWN while reduction,
monitoring, heartbeat and alert retry remain alive.

The closed operating envelope is: one selected ticker; dedicated account with
only declared capital and no unrelated cash, positions, orders or manual
activity; manual market replacement; no claim of automatic programme rotation.
Required evidence is a green read-only qualification, clean S=1 first-fill
canary, clean attended S=12 burn-in, final scenario/invariant and operational
readiness, exact full promotion gate, active external dead man, and explicit
operator review.

New work blocks CR-1 only after adjudication that its failure is reachable in
this operating envelope or that CR-1 acceptance cannot be evidenced without it.
Priority labels alone do not move the finish line. Dynamic selection, rotation
and automatic management of unrelated held markets belong to CR-2; CR-1 instead
refuses a dirty account and stops on foreign activity.

Acceptance: record exact commit, config/rung, assignment window, dedicated-
account check, supervision state, runbook/drill evidence and links to all three
promotion rungs. After closure, repeated cycles are authorised only inside that
assignment.

dependencies.title: fee_cost is parsed with ParsePrice4; 6-decimal fees discard every fills walk and block q01
dependencies.description:
The fills walk applies the PRICE parser to `fee_cost`, and fees carry a finer
quantum than prices. Every complete fills walk on this account is therefore
discarded, the fills freshness clock never advances, and q01's portfolio
freshness bar can never be met.

MEASURED 2026-08-12 on the first real q01 attempt (candidate dc77e3f, binary
sha256 1882b82f..., ticker KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE). Three minutes in:

  monitor    observed 60  fresh 60            -- fine
  portfolio  observed 12  fresh_complete 0  incomplete_walks 12

Every single portfolio walk incomplete, one FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE anomaly per 5s
poll. q01 requires >= 99% fresh+complete portfolio slots; the run sat at 0% and
could not recover, so it was stopped rather than left to burn six hours into a
guaranteed assessment failure.

THE CHAIN

  harness/wsx/portfolio.go:564  fee4, err := rest.ParsePrice4(f.FeeCost)
  harness/rest/read.go:50       len(fracPart) > 4 -> error, "this parser will
                                not round"
  harness/wsx/portfolio.go:399  convertFills error -> FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE SEV1,
                                eff.Stop = true, whole result discarded

The offending value is real exchange data: fill 1582884a-1f64-7c20-fab4-b40468ad5df6
has fee_cost "0.017200" -- six decimals. ParsePrice4's measured quantum is 1e-4
dollars, which is right for PRICES. It is not right for fees: a fee is a
fraction of a price and is quoted finer. The defect is applying a price parser
to a fee field, not the parser's strictness.

NOT WORKAROUNDABLE OPERATIONALLY. The fill is historical and sits on the real
account, so it appears in every complete fills walk forever. There is no config
knob, no ticker change and no restart that avoids it. q01 CANNOT RUN on this
account until this is fixed.

THE PARSER BEHAVED CORRECTLY. read.go's own comment says "Truncating here would
silently discard precision the exchange chose to send. If the quantum ever gets
finer, this must surface as an error and be handled, not rounded away." That is
exactly what happened: it surfaced, loudly, through the real alert channel, on a
read-only run, before any writer existed. This is the qualification doing its
job.

FIX. Give fees their own conversion rather than widening ParsePrice4 -- prices
and fees have different measured quanta and collapsing them would lose the
assertion that makes ParsePrice4 useful. Measure the actual fee quantum from
live data before choosing the width. H-ORD-8 uses fee_cost as its INDEPENDENT
check (portfolio.go:551), so whatever type it becomes must keep that comparison
meaningful.

SEQUENCING. This forces a gate round before q01 can be attempted again, so
lip-83o (the launchd plist boolean defect) should ride along in the SAME round
rather than being worked around a second time.
dependencies.notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 by go/cmd/conform, read-only, against the real account. This settles the type question the description left open.

THE FEE QUANTUM IS 1e-6 DOLLARS, and it is not occasional. All 15 fills in account history carry fee_cost with EXACTLY six decimal places -- the decimal-place histogram is {6: 15}, with no other width present. Eight distinct values appear and ParsePrice4 refuses every one of them, INCLUDING "0.000000": the refusal is on width, not magnitude, so a zero fee is just as unconvertible as a large one. There is no subset of this account history on which the current parser succeeds, which is why every complete walk was discarded rather than most of them.

THE TARGET TYPE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY CORRECT. wsx/portfolio.go:577 writes Fee: num.Money(fee4 * 100) with the comment "Money is 1e-6 dollars and a Price4 is 1e-4 dollars". So the destination is already a 1e-6 quantity and the code is upcasting into it -- the only wrong step is routing the string through a 1e-4 parser first. Parsing fee_cost directly into num.Money at 1e-6 removes the conversion rather than adding one, and leaves ParsePrice4 untouched so its 1e-4 assertion keeps its meaning, which the description asked for.

H-ORD-8 COMPARISON PRESERVED: portfolio.go:551 uses fee_cost as S2s independent corroborator via Fee > 0. A 1e-6 parse keeps that exact comparison and makes it sharper, since a fee below 1e-4 currently has nowhere to land.

SEVERITY IS UNDERSTATED ABOVE. The description says the freshness clock never advances and q01 cannot meet its bar. What actually happens is worse: eff.Stop reaches run.go:1315 requestStop("portfolio_read"), the global machine goes RUNNING -> WINDING_DOWN -> DRAINED, and quote/machine.go:451 states there is NO transition back to RUNNING without an operator action. Attempt 1s evidence confirms it -- global=DRAINED for 22,547 state samples starting 2.3s after launch, against 51 samples of RUNNING;QUOTING over the first 0.3s. q01 attempt 1 was not slowly failing a bar; it was permanently halted at t+2.3s and spent its remaining 3m22s drained. Everything downstream of a SUCCESSFUL portfolio walk -- adoption, quoting, rung behaviour, the H-checks, multi-hour freshness -- has therefore never executed against real data at all.

BLOCKED BY A SECOND DEFECT ON THE SAME FILLS: see lip-jhi. Eight of these fifteen fills are is_taker=true with non-zero fees, and the first thing that happens once the fee parses is TAKER_FILL -> eff.Stop -> the same durable halt. Fixing this bead alone moves the halt one layer deeper without moving it later. The two must ship together.
dependencies.close_reason: Implemented, tested and covered by new catalogue mutations; tree green on build, vet, gofmt, check.py and go test -race. Full write-ups are in each bead's notes. Not yet through a full gate round -- lip-b0t and lip-rj5 remain open in the same batch.

dependencies.title: q01 operator proof: real alert and missed dead-man alarm
dependencies.description: Perform the external alert actions that code and a local evidence bundle cannot self-attest. Using the exact q01 candidate and configured production alert collaborators, receive one real test notification and deliberately withhold a dead-man check-in long enough for the external provider to alarm. Preserve provider-side timestamps and the notification/alarm artifacts. This bead is an operator action: no agent runs cmd/harness against the live account or claims provider behavior from local counters.
dependencies.acceptance_criteria: Attach the exact candidate commit/config identity, one delivered real notification, one deliberately missed check-in, and provider-side proof that the independent alarm fired within its configured window. Redact opaque endpoints and bearer secrets. Any missing/late alarm blocks q01.
dependencies.notes:
Candidate identity this alert proof belongs to (prepared 2026-08-12, proof not
yet performed).

  nominated commit  dc77e3f  (the commit lip-jy4 closed GREEN, 273/273)
  binary            /Users/hugh/.lip/bin/harness
  binary sha256     1882b82fbec9c00aeb683086fb2d1e11a86cbcd7fff0462b96dfba3fdd8d0cf1
  config            /Users/hugh/.lip/canary/config.json
  ticker            KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE
  runbook           /Users/hugh/.lip/q01-runbook.md  (step 2)

The three secrets in ~/.kalshi/env were already loaded and validated through the
real production loaders (ping.LoadNTFYTopic, ping.LoadHTTPSDeadman); DEADMAN_URL
is https with a host. What remains is the part code cannot self-attest.

DELIVERED NOTIFICATION. Sent to the same base URL and headers the production
sender uses -- POST https://ntfy.sh/<topic> with Title and Priority headers
(harness/ping/ntfy.go:16,105-119) -- with the topic read from the same env file
and never printed. Priority: urgent is the SEV1 vocabulary, and it is the reason
Section 13.1 stays on ntfy: lip-e28 was closed NOT DOING because email has no
equivalent and cannot wake a sleeping operator.

MISSED CHECK-IN. The healthchecks period is temporarily 5 min / grace 1 min so
the alarm lands in about 6 minutes instead of 80, then restored to 1 hour /
20 min before q01 -- which matches heartbeat_s, whose default is 3600s
(harness/cfg/params.go:163).

Two ordering facts that decide whether this proof is valid at all:

  - The check MUST be pinged once before the check-in is withheld. A
    healthchecks check that has never been pinged stays "new" and never alarms,
    so withholding against a never-pinged check proves nothing and would produce
    a screenshot of silence.
  - The check must be pinged again after the window is restored, so q01 does not
    start into an already-firing alarm.

The q01 restart drill will not spuriously alarm. Service.Step treats
lastHeartbeatMs == 0 as due (harness/ping/service.go:306), so every fresh
process checks in immediately; a restart resets the dead-man clock rather than
extending it. The q01 process's own startup heartbeat therefore also delivers a
real ntfy push from the candidate binary through the production loader -- worth
capturing as corroboration on this bead, since it is notification delivery by
the exact candidate rather than by a hand-built request.

CLOSED 2026-08-12 on operator attestation, WITHOUT the provider-side artifacts
the acceptance criteria ask for. Recording the gap here so a later reader does
not mistake this closure for the evidence being on file.

What was performed, via `~/.lip/q01.sh alert-proof` against candidate dc77e3f
(binary sha256 1882b82f..., config KXMAMDANIMENTION-26AUG12-SAFE):

  - healthchecks window temporarily tightened to period 5 min / grace 1 min
  - one real notification POSTed to the production ntfy channel with
    Priority: urgent, topic read from ~/.kalshi/env and never printed;
    the script requires HTTP 200 before continuing
  - one dead-man check-in delivered, so the check went UP rather than staying
    "new" (a never-pinged check never alarms)
  - the next check-in deliberately withheld for ~7 minutes
  - window restored to period 1 hour / grace 20 min and the check cleared

Operator reports the notification arrived and the alarm fired. NOT PRESERVED:
the phone screenshot of the delivered notification, and the provider-side
screenshot of the alarm with its timestamp and the missed check-in in the event
log. So the alarm's firing is attested by the operator rather than evidenced by
the provider.

Consequence for lip-q01, which depends on this bead: q01's acceptance criteria
require "proof that the external missed-heartbeat alarm fired", and
AssessQ01Local always prints "alert-provider receipt and proof that a
missed-heartbeat alarm fired" in external_outstanding because no local counter
can establish it. That item will therefore still be outstanding when q01 is
assessed, and closing q01 will rest on the same attestation.

This is recoverable at no cost if wanted later: healthchecks.io retains the
check's event log, so the missed check-in and the alarm remain screenshottable
after the fact. Reopen and attach if the evidence bundle is ever audited.

Notification-delivery evidence captured after closure, and it is stronger than the hand-built curl: ~/.lip/evidence/2026-08-12-ntfy-sev1-fill-unconvertible.png is a phone screenshot of three real alerts pushed by the CANDIDATE BINARY itself (dc77e3f, sha256 1882b82f...) through the production ntfy channel during the first q01 attempt at 10:30 local / 17:30Z -- a SEV1 FILL_UNCONVERTIBLE at urgent priority (red chevrons visible), a SEV2 RESNAPSHOT_DEFERRED, and the STARTUP summary. Each carries its own first-seen timestamp and anomaly id. This evidences the delivery half of this bead by the exact candidate rather than by a curl. It does NOT evidence the missed dead-man alarm, which remains operator-attested; healthchecks.io retains that event log if it is ever wanted.
dependencies.close_reason: Operator performed the alert proof against dc77e3f: real ntfy notification delivered and the external dead-man alarmed on a deliberately withheld check-in. Closed on operator attestation; provider-side screenshots not preserved (see notes).
